summary: Tiered off-ramp & validation plan for aggressive batching + mixed-precision quant enabled by tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer enabled a high-aggression optimizer profile for tenant mediscale-dedicated that turns on async aggregation batching, KV prefix caching and mixed-precision quantization (q4/q8 hybrid) during a traffic increase window. Within 45 minutes they reported increased 5xx rate for long-stream sessions and a subtle accuracy drift on their evaluation prompts. Customer asks for a conservative, validated off-ramp and verification steps to de-escalate without losing cached benefits for other tenants.

Impact:
- 8% request 5xx increase for long streaming sessions (>= 120s) for mediscale-dedicated.
- Slight accuracy drift observed on scheduled prompt-eval set (A/B drift ~1.8% BLEU-like proxy).
- Potential customer-visible failures in production chat flows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: mediscale-dedicated (reserved capacity, us-east)
- Runtime version: 2.14.3
- Optimizer profile: mediscale-aggressive-2026-03-10
- Traffic pattern: peak window 09:00-11:00 ET, average seq_len 512, 75% streaming sessions

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Pin tenant to mediscale-aggressive-2026-03-10 optimizer profile.
2) Synthesize 2k sessions with streaming enabled and sequence distribution matching production.
3) Observe backend 5xx count and eval prompt scoring differences between baseline profile and aggressive profile.

Observed behavior:
- Backend shows elevated 5xxs originating from serving-runtime process restarts and memory pressure evictions on some GPUs.
- KV cache hit rate increased for short sessions but for long sessions the async batching pipeline leads to increased tail latency and occasional stream disconnects.
- Eval set scoring shows small but measurable accuracy regression.

Expected behavior:
- No material increase in 5xx rate after safe optimizer tuning. Any degradation should be gated behind tenant-weighted canary and metric alarms.

Logs and evidence provided by customer (truncated):
- SRE trace: https://observability.redwood.com/trace/mediscale/trace-20260310-09
- Prometheus dash: https://observability.redwood.com/d/tenant/mediscale-dedicated-optimizer
- Customer eval diff CSV attached to ticket (uploaded to ticket attachments).

Investigation notes (support/engineering):
- Initial hypothesis: mixed-precision path (q4 fallback to q8 for specific kernels) combined with async aggregation batching changed memory allocation pattern and introduced sporadic OOM/eviction on older A100s in pool.
- Evidence: kube node OOM events correlate with 5xx spikes, GPU memory fragmentation metrics show higher variance after optimizer profile applied.
- Secondary hypothesis: long streaming sessions interact poorly with batch aggregation cutoff (batch window set at 40ms) causing head-of-line blocking and increased tail latency.
- Checked rollout: profile was enabled for 100% of mediscale traffic at 08:45 without staged canary.

Support actions taken so far:
- Opened INT escalation with infra (INT-1123) to check GPU memory fragmentation and kernel allocation traces.
- Temporarily reduced aggregation window for mediscale tenant to 12ms (hotfix) to reduce head-of-line impact while we plan off-ramp.
- Captured optimizer profile snapshot and created immediate backup of tenant routing config.
- Collected sample traces and heap profiles for analysis (links in investigation notes).

Recommended tiered off-ramp & validation plan (stepwise, conservative):
1) Stage 1 — Traffic gating and monitoring (5-15 minutes):
   - Create a 90/10 traffic split: 90% traffic still to current profile, 10% to a fallback profile with only batching disabled (keep KV caching + quantization).
   - Add short-window SLI alarms for 5xx, P95 latency, and eval-proxy scoring drift.
   - Duration: 10 minutes.
2) Stage 2 — Partial demotion (10-30 minutes):
   - Move to 50/50 split between aggressive profile and fallback_no_batch (fallback retains quantization).
   - Observe memory evictions and streaming disconnects.
   - If 5xx improves >50% and drift reduces, continue to next stage; else continue rollback to baseline.
3) Stage 3 — Quantization holdpoint (30-60 minutes):
   - If issues persist, disable mixed-precision quantization (fall back to q8 path) while keeping prefix caching and batch window conservative (12ms).
   - Run a small set (100 requests) of customer eval prompts via console to validate accuracy.
4) Stage 4 — Full demote to baseline (if required):
   - Revert tenant to baseline safe profile (pre-2026-03-10) and keep traffic split 100% to baseline.
   - Run wider validation (2k evals) and postmortem.

Validation checklist to run after each stage (automatable):
- Compare 5xx rate and streaming disconnects (target: <= baseline + 1%).
- Sample model outputs on canonical prompt set and compute evaluation proxy score.
- Verify GPU OOM/eviction counts and memory fragmentation percentiles.
- Confirm no unexpected increase in cost per token beyond planned thresholds.

Safe commands & quick actions (console/CLI):
- Snapshot current optimizer profile: redwoodctl optimizer snapshot --tenant mediscale-dedicated --name before-offramp-2026-03-10
- Create traffic split: redwoodctl routing split --tenant mediscale-dedicated --from aggressive-profile --to fallback-no-batch --ratio 90:10
- Disable quant path flag for tenant: redwoodctl feature-flag set --tenant mediscale-dedicated --flag quant_mixed_precision=false
- Restore baseline: redwoodctl tenant pin --tenant mediscale-dedicated --profile baseline-20260228

Automation & follow-up items assigned to engineering:
- Add a holdpoint guard to optimizer rollouts so profiles that enable both async aggregation and mixed-precision require a staged canary by default. (ENG-PRIORITY: high)
- Improve memory fragmentation telemetry per GPU and add alarm thresholds. (ENG-PRIORITY: medium)

Customer asks in ticket:
- A step-by-step safe rollback that minimizes customer-visible impact.
- Verification commands that they can run from their side to confirm accuracy after each stage.
- A postmortem once root cause identified.

Resolution plan proposed to customer (pending approval):
- Execute recommended tiered off-ramp during off-peak window tomorrow 03-13 02:00-04:00 ET with SRE and customer on call.
- Provide scripted CLI steps and a short-runbook tailored to their tenant.
- Commit to a short postmortem within 48 hours of full demotion and remediation timeline for runtime fixes.

Attachments: list of traces, eval CSV, optimizer profile snapshot IDs available in ticket attachments and linked Confluence page.
